introduction.summary: This specification records the project purpose, stakeholder constraints and unresolved decisions stated in the source evidence below.

items.title: Stakeholder project context
items.detail: Build a campus wireless network access-control requirements specification.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-002
items.detail: Students and guests may access the internet but must not access the internal staff network.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-003

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-004
items.detail: Security operators may review and acknowledge alerts but may not change access policies.

requirements.title: Students and guests may access the internet but must not access the internal staff network.
requirements.statement: Students and guests may access the internet but must not access the internal staff network.

acceptance_criteria.given: A student device connected to the public network
acceptance_criteria.when: The student attempts to access the internet
acceptance_criteria.then: The request is granted and connectivity is established
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of successful internet access response

acceptance_criteria.given: A guest device connected to the public network
acceptance_criteria.when: The guest attempts to access the internal staff network
acceptance_criteria.then: The request is denied and no connection is established
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of firewall denial packet for internal staff network

unresolved_decisions: Whether 'access' implies only direct connectivity or includes proxy-based routes

requirements.title: Network administrators may manually isolate a device and restore its access.
requirements.statement: Network administrators may manually isolate a device and restore its access.

acceptance_criteria.given: An administrator with valid credentials and a device under management
acceptance_criteria.when: The administrator initiates manual isolation of the device via console interface
acceptance_criteria.then: The device is isolated and status changes to 'isolated' in system state
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of device isolation command execution and resulting state update

acceptance_criteria.given: An administrator with valid credentials and a device under management
acceptance_criteria.when: The administrator initiates manual restoration of access to the device
acceptance_criteria.then: Access is restored and device status changes to 'active'
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of access restoration command execution and resulting state update

unresolved_decisions: Whether restoration must be confirmed by a second operator or audit log

requirements.title: Do not automatically change firewall rules or isolate devices.
requirements.statement: Do not automatically change firewall rules or isolate devices.

acceptance_criteria.given: A test device in active network state with no prior isolation
acceptance_criteria.when: The system attempts to automatically isolate the device via scheduled rule update or trigger event
acceptance_criteria.then: No isolation occurs and the device remains in active state
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of firewall configuration before and after; no change detected

acceptance_criteria.given: A test device with active connection and configured rules
acceptance_criteria.when: The system attempts to automatically modify firewall rules to restrict access
acceptance_criteria.then: No rule modification occurs and the existing rules remain unchanged
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of firewall configuration before and after; no change detected

unresolved_decisions: Whether automatic actions are triggered by specific events (e.g., traffic anomalies) or time-based schedules

nonfunctional.applicability_reason: Existing canonical requirements, where applicable, are linked below; this section adds no separate obligation. Unresolved stakeholder decisions remain open.

security.applicability_reason: Source-backed obligations; unspecified decisions remain open.

requirements.title: Security operators may review and acknowledge alerts but may not change access policies.
requirements.statement: Security operators may review and acknowledge alerts but may not change access policies.

acceptance_criteria.given: An operator with security privileges and an active alert in the system
acceptance_criteria.then: The system returns a successful acknowledgement response indicating the alert is acknowledged
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of the acknowledgment response from the system

acceptance_criteria.given: An operator with security privileges and an active access policy rule
acceptance_criteria.when: The operator attempts to modify the access policy
acceptance_criteria.then: The system denies the modification request and returns a permission denied error
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of the denial response when attempting to modify policies

acceptance_criteria.given: The operator receives an alert for access policy change
acceptance_criteria.when: The operator initiates the review action
acceptance_criteria.then: The system confirms the alert is acknowledged and no access policy modification occurs
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of resulting state shows the alert status updated to 'acknowledged' without any change to access policies, as verified by a real-time policy integrity check

unresolved_decisions: Definition of 'acknowledged' state in alert lifecycle

requirements.title: The system must record administrator policy changes and retain audit records for 30 days.
requirements.statement: The system must record administrator policy changes and retain audit records for 30 days.

acceptance_criteria.given: An administrator performs a policy change operation
acceptance_criteria.when: The system logs the policy change event
acceptance_criteria.then: The audit record is stored in the system and remains accessible for 30 days after creation
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of audit records retrieved after 30 days from change timestamp

acceptance_criteria.given: The system has recorded an administrator policy change
acceptance_criteria.when: The system attempts to return the record
acceptance_criteria.then: The system retains audit records for 30 days
acceptance_criteria.observable_evidence: Test capture of resulting state shows audit records retained for 30 days in the log repository with no data loss or corruption over time, as verified by a compliance inspection report from E-005_test_

unresolved_decisions: Exact retention period boundary (e.g., calendar day vs. system time)
The source gives a retention duration; minimum/maximum interpretation and deletion timing remain unconfirmed.

glossary.summary: Source-present terminology; definitions introduce no additional product obligation.

items.title: Access control
items.detail: Rules and enforcement governing which principals may perform actions on resources.

items.title: Policy
items.detail: A rule or decision governing permitted actions; its project-specific meaning remains defined by the source requirements.

items.title: Audit record
items.detail: A stored record of an event. Required event scope and retention are determined by the linked source, not this definition.

items.title: Device isolation
items.detail: Restriction of a device's network access; the source determines whether and by whom this action is permitted.

items.title: Access restoration
items.detail: Returning access that was previously restricted, within the source-defined permission boundary.

items.title: Concurrency
items.detail: Activity occurring at the same time; it is distinct from the registered planning population.

items.title: Registered population
items.detail: The inventory of registered users or devices; it does not by itself establish a simultaneous load or a maximum.

items.title: Retention
items.detail: The period or rule for keeping records. A bare duration does not itself specify deletion timing or minimum/maximum bounds.

items.title: Firewall
items.detail: A control that permits or restricts network traffic according to rules; mentioning it does not authorize automatic changes.

sdlc.justification: The evolving stability (E-008) and frequent feedback (E-008) favor Agile because it enables iterative delivery, continuous adaptation, and rapid response to changing requirements. The absence of budget, failure consequences, or legacy systems makes Hybrid, Incremental, DevSecOps, Spiral, V-Model, and Waterfall less suitable due to insufficient differentiating evidence. No evidence supports budget, delivery, uncertainty, verification, regulation, schedule, or failure consequence thresholds.
tradeoffs: Recurring delivery requires stakeholder review and backlog refinement; a cycle does not guarantee completeness or remove unresolved decisions.
